notes: Fixed the focal/auxiliary queries to literally follow the assigned route CONVERSATION->WORKSPACE->WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP (channels->teams->user_teams) as the backbone, then extend from the qualifying admin's user_teams row through users to the participant table (channel_members / messages / message_reactions->messages) and close the loop by revisiting 'channels' as the terminal node, which the engine binds back to the root channel (node0). This correctly restricts matches to channels where the SAME admin user_teams-holder is directly a channel member, message author, or reaction contributor on that specific channel, rather than merely sharing a workspace. Recomputation with this structure yields exactly the three intended matches (C01ABCD1234 general, C02EFGH5678 random, C03IJKL9012 engineering) via Robert Walsh's memberships/authorship, while Morgan Freeman (admin, no participation anywhere) contributes nothing, and Robert Chen's memberships (core-infra, model-research, product-growth, frontend, project-alpha-dev) and the growth channel remain correctly excluded since none of their participants hold an admin workspace-membership role. No seed edits were needed since all required facts were already present in the base seed. All match/negative channels are public, non-DM, non-archived channels in the single workspace, so ordinary conversations.list/history/members/reactions.get access suffices for solver discovery without extra memberships.
